Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 38, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surah Sad

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah), it has already been covered at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here.

* *

His saying: ﴿By the Qur'an, full of reminder﴾ means: by the Qur'an, which contains that which is a reminder for the servants and a benefit for them in this world and the next.

Al-Dahhak said, regarding His words ﴿full of reminder﴾, that it is like His saying: ﴿We have certainly sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder﴾ [al-Anbiya' 10], meaning: your admonition. Qatadah said likewise, and Ibn Jarir preferred this view.

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, Ibn 'Uyaynah, Abu Husayn, Abu Salih and al-Suddi said: ﴿full of reminder﴾ means full of honour, that is, of rank and standing.

There is no contradiction between the two views, for it is a noble Book containing admonition, warning and alarm.

They differed concerning the response (jawab) to this oath. Some said it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, each one [of them] did not but deny the messengers, so My penalty was deserved﴾ [Sad 14]. It was also said that it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is true—the dispute of the people of the Fire﴾ [Sad 64]. Ibn Jarir related both views, and this second one is far-fetched; Ibn Jarir also deemed it weak.

Qatadah said: its response is: ﴿Rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition﴾, and Ibn Jarir preferred this.

It was also said: its response is what the context of the whole surah implies, and Allah knows best.

Then Ibn Jarir related from some scholars of the Arabic language that he said: its response is "Sad", meaning: "truth is true, and by the Qur'an full of reminder".

* *

His saying: ﴿Rather, those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition﴾ means: indeed, in this Qur'an there is a reminder for whoever takes heed, and a lesson for whoever takes admonition. The disbelievers have not benefited from it only because they are ﴿in arrogance﴾, that is, pride and refusal to accept it, ﴿and opposition﴾, that is, defiance, enmity and separation from it.

Then He warned them of what destroyed the nations that denied before them, because of their opposition to the messengers and their denial of the Books sent down from heaven. He said: ﴿How many generations We destroyed before them﴾, that is, how many a denying community, ﴿and they called out﴾, that is, when the punishment came upon them they sought help and cried out to Allah. But that did not avail them anything, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they perceived Our might, at once they fled from it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 12], that is, they ran away, ﴿Do not run, and return to that in which you were given luxury and your dwellings; perhaps you will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 13].

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah narrated to us from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the saying of Allah: ﴿And they called out, but it was not a time for escape﴾. He said: "It was not a time for calling out, nor for leaping, nor for fleeing." [It has been narrated by al-Tabari in the Masa'il of Nafi' ibn al-Azraq that he asked Ibn 'Abbas, and so he mentioned it.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "It was not a time for rescue."

Shabib ibn Bishr related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, when he was asked: "They called out the call when it would no longer benefit them," and he recited:

*Layla reminded him, but it was not the time for reminding,*
*And he had repented of her, though escape was far off.* [The verse is by al-A'sha; its second half is: "And he had repented of her, though escape was far off."]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding His saying: ﴿And they called out, but it was not a time for escape﴾: they called out with monotheism when the world turned away from them, and they sought refuge in repentance when the world turned away from them.

Qatadah said: when they saw the punishment, they wanted to repent, but it was not the time for calling out.

Mujahid said: ﴿And they called out, but it was not a time for escape﴾: it was not a time for fleeing, nor for an answer.

Something similar has been narrated from 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Hasan and Qatadah.

From Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿but it was not a time for escape﴾, and there is no calling out at a time other than the time of calling out.

This word, "lat" (لات), is the negative "la" to which the "ta'" has been added, just as it is added to "thumma" so that they say "thummat," and to "rubba" so that they say "rubbat." It is written separately, and the pause falls upon it. Some have related from the Imam Mushaf, as mentioned by [Ibn Jarir] [the bracketed text is blank in one manuscript] that it is joined to "hin" as "wa-la tahin manas." The well-known view is the first. The majority then read "hin" in the accusative, its implied sense being: "and the time is not a time of escape." Some permitted the accusative with it, and recited:

*Layla's love reminded him, but it was not the time—*
*And grey hair has now cut off the companion.* [The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (23/77).]

Some permitted the genitive with it, and recited:

*They sought our reconciliation, but it was not the time,*
*So we answered that there is no time for survival.* [The verse is by Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i, and is in Tafsir al-Tabari (23/77).] Some also recited:

*And it was not the hour of regret,*

with the genitive on "sa'ah" (ساعة). The people of the language say: "al-naws" is retreat, and "al-bawš" is advance. For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and it was not a time for escape﴾, that is, the time is not a time for fleeing or for departing.

The Almighty says, reporting about the polytheists and their astonishment at the Messenger being a human being, as He said: ﴿Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them, "Warn the people and give glad tidings to those who believe that they have a sure standing with their Lord"? The disbelievers said, "This is indeed a clear magician."﴾ Here He said: ﴿And they wondered that a warner had come to them from among themselves﴾, meaning a human being like them. ﴿And the disbelievers said, "This is a lying magician. Has he made the gods into one God? This is indeed a strange thing!"﴾, meaning: does he claim that the object of worship is one, that there is no god but Him? The polytheists denied this, may Allah disfigure them, and they marvelled at abandoning association with Allah, for they had inherited the worship of idols from their fathers, and it had been soaked into their hearts. When the Messenger ﷺ called them to remove that from their hearts and to single out Allah in oneness, they found this monstrous and were astonished, and said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ And ﴿the chiefs among them set off﴾, namely their nobles, leaders, heads and elders, saying: ﴿"Go on, and be steadfast for your gods."﴾, meaning: persist in your religion, ﴿and do not respond to what Muhammad calls you to of monotheism.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is something intended﴾, Ibn Jarir said: Indeed, this which Muhammad ﷺ calls us to, of monotheism, is something he intends by it to gain superiority over you and dominance, and for himself to have followers from among you, and we will not respond to him.

The reason for the revelation of these verses:

Al-Suddi said: Some people of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, along with a group of the elders of Quraysh. Some of them said to others: "Come, let us go to Abu Talib and speak with him about this, so that he may act justly with us regarding him, and he will stop reviling our gods, and we will leave him and his God whom he worships. For we fear that this old man will die and then something from us will come upon him." The Arabs would reproach us: "They left him until, when his uncle died, they assailed him." So they sent a man from among them called al-Mutallib, and he asked permission for them to enter upon Abu Talib. He said: "These are the elders of your people and their chiefs, asking permission to see you." He said: "Let them enter." When they entered upon him, they said: "O Abu Talib, you are our senior and our master, so deal justly with us regarding your nephew. Order him to stop reviling our gods, and we will leave him and his God." He said: So Abu Talib sent for him, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon him, he said: "O my nephew, these are the elders of your people and their chiefs, and they have asked you to stop reviling their gods, and they will leave you and your God." He said: "O uncle, shall I not call them to what is better for them?" He said: "And to what will you call them?" He said: "I call them to say a single word by which the Arabs will submit to them and by which they will rule the non-Arabs." Abu Jahl said from among the people: "What is it, by your father? We will give it to you and ten times its like." He said: "You say: 'There is no god but Allah.'" So they recoiled and said: "Ask us for something other than this." He said: "Even if you brought me the sun to place in my hand, I would not ask you for anything other than it." So they rose from his presence in anger, saying: "By Allah, we will revile you and the God who commanded you with this." And ﴿the chiefs among them set off, saying, "Go on, and be steadfast for your gods. Indeed, this is something intended."﴾

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, who added: When they had left, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called his uncle to the saying "There is no god but Allah," but he refused and said: "Rather, [I remain] on the religion of the elders." And there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ [al-Qasas: 56]. [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/80).]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb and Ibn WakI' narrated to us, both saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abbad narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Abu Talib fell ill, a group of Quraysh entered upon him, among them Abu Jahl, and they said: "Your nephew reviles our gods, and does this and that, and says this and that. Would you not send for him and forbid him?" So he sent for him, and the Prophet ﷺ came and entered the house, and between them and Abu Talib was the space of a man's seat. He said: Abu Jahl feared that if he sat beside Abu Talib, he would be softened toward him. So he leapt up and sat in that place, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ found no seat near his uncle, so he sat by the door. Abu Talib said to him: "O my nephew, what is the matter with your people, complaining about you? They claim that you revile their gods and say this and that." He said: They pressed him with much talk, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke and said: "O uncle, I want them to [agree to] one word! They will say it, and the Arabs will submit to them by it, and the non-Arabs will pay them the tribute." So they were alarmed by his word and his speech, and they said: "One word! Yes, by your father, ten!" They said: "And what is it?" Abu Talib said: "And what word is it, O my nephew?" He said: "There is no god but Allah." So they stood up alarmed, shaking their garments, and saying: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ He said: And from this place there was revealed [the verses] up to His saying: ﴿they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾. The wording is that of Abu Kurayb. [Tafsir al-Tabari (23/79).]

Thus Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated it, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr, both of them from Abu Usamah, from al-A'mash, from Abbad, without attribution (ghayr mansub), with similar wording. [Al-Musnad (1/362) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11437.] Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also narrated it, all in their tafsirs, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Umara al-Kufi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Tirmidhi said: it is hasan (good). [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3232, al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11436, and Tafsir al-Tabari (23/79).]

* *

As for their saying: ﴿We have not heard of this in the last religion﴾, meaning: we have not heard of this which Muhammad calls us to, of monotheism, in the last religion.

Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: They mean the religion of Quraysh.

Others said: They mean Christianity. This was said by Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Suddi.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿We have not heard of this in the last religion﴾: he meant Christianity. They said: "If this Qur'an were true, the Christians would have informed us of it."

﴿This is nothing but a fabrication﴾: Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is a lie. Ibn Abbas said: it is an invention (takharrus).

* *

As for their saying: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾, meaning: they find it improbable that he should be singled out for the revelation of the Qur'an from among all of them, just as they said in another verse: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31]. Allah the Almighty said: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32]. Therefore, when they said this, which indicated their ignorance and the feebleness of their intellect in finding it improbable that the Qur'an should be sent down upon the Messenger from among them, Allah the Almighty said: ﴿Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾, meaning: they only say this because until the time of their saying it they have not tasted the punishment of Allah and His vengeance. They will soon know the outcome of what they said, and of what they denied, on the day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell with a violent push.

Then He said, explaining that He is the one who disposes of His dominion, the Doer of what He wills, who gives whom He wills what He wills, honours whom He wills, humbles whom He wills, guides whom He wills, leads astray whom He wills, sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, and seals the heart of whom He wills, so no one can guide him after Allah. Indeed, the servants do not possess anything of the command, nor do they have any disposal over the dominion, not even the weight of an atom, nor do they possess a speck (qitmir). Therefore Allah the Almighty said, rebuking them: ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower?﴾, meaning: the Mighty whose presence cannot be approached, the Bestower who gives what He wills to whom He wills.

This verse is similar to His saying: ﴿Or do they have a share in the dominion? Then they would not give people even a speck. Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great dominion. So they sent a man from among them called al-Mutallib, and he asked permission for them to enter upon Abu Talib. He said: "These are the elders of your people and their chiefs, asking permission to see you." He said: "Let them enter." When they entered upon him, they said: "O Abu Talib, you are our senior and our master, so deal justly with us regarding your nephew. He said: So Abu Talib sent for him, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon him, he said: "O my nephew, these are the elders of your people and their chiefs, and they have asked you to stop reviling their gods, and they will leave you and your God." He said: Abu Jahl feared that if he sat beside Abu Talib, he would be softened toward him. Abu Talib said to him: "O my nephew, what is the matter with your people, complaining about you? They claim that you revile their gods and say this and that." This Cry is the Blast of Terror, which Allah commands Israfil to prolong, so that none in the heavens and the earth remains without being terrified, except whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, exempts.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 38, verses 17–20:

God mentions His servant and messenger Dawud (peace be upon him), that he was ﴿possessed of strength﴾. Al-ayd means strength in knowledge and in action.

[Ibn ʿAbbas] [[Addition from T, S.]] and Ibn Zayd and al-Suddi said: al-ayd means strength. Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿And the heaven We built with strength, and indeed We are expanding it﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47].

Mujahid said: al-ayd means strength in obedience.

Qatadah said: Dawud (peace be upon him) [[Addition from T, S, A.]] was given strength in worship and understanding of the religion. It has been related to us that he (peace be upon him) would stand in prayer for a third of the night and fast for half of the time.

This is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "The most beloved prayer to God is the prayer of Dawud, and the most beloved fasting to God is the fasting of Dawud. He would sleep half the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. He would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would not flee when he met (the enemy)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1131), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1159).]] And he was ʾawwab, meaning one who returns to God, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his affairs and matters.

* *

God's saying: ﴿Indeed We subjected the mountains to glorify (God) with him at evening and at sunrise﴾. That is, God subjected the mountains to glorify God along with him at sunrise and at the end of the day, as He said: ﴿O mountains, echo His praises along with him, and (you) birds﴾ [Saba': 10]. Likewise, the birds would glorify God in accordance with his glorification and echo his chanting. When a bird passed by him while it was gliding in the air and heard him chanting the recitation of the Zabur (Psalms), it could not go on; rather, it would stop in the air and glorify God along with him, and the lofty mountains would answer him, echoing with him and glorifying in accordance with him.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAbd al-Karim, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, [[In T: "with its isnad".]] from Ibn ʿAbbas [[In A: "Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both".]] that it reached him: that Umm Hani mentioned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest of Makkah prayed the forenoon prayer (duha) eight rakʿahs. [[In T: "Then he said".]] Ibn ʿAbbas said: "I had thought that this time has a prayer, and God, the Exalted, says: ﴿They glorify (Him) at evening and at sunrise﴾."

Then he related it from the hadith of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Safwan, from his client ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn [[In A: "from".]] Nawfal, that Ibn ʿAbbas used not to pray the forenoon prayer. He said: "I took him to Umm Hani and said: 'Tell him what you told me.'" Umm Hani said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon me in my house on the day of the conquest. He then ordered water to be poured into a bowl, then ordered a cloth, which he held between me and him, and he washed. Then he sprinkled a corner of the house and prayed eight rakʿahs. Their standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting were all equal, close to one another." So Ibn ʿAbbas went out saying: "I have read what is between the two covers (of the Qur'an), and I did not know the forenoon prayer until now: ﴿They glorify (Him) at evening and at sunrise﴾." And he used to say: "Where is the prayer of ishraq?" Afterwards he would say: "The prayer of ishraq." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/87).]]

Therefore He said: ﴿And the birds gathered﴾, that is, held back in the air, ﴿each one returning to Him﴾, that is, obedient, glorifying in accordance with him.

Said ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿each one returning to Him﴾ means obedient.

[And His saying] [[Addition from T, S, A.]] ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾, that is, We gave him a complete kingdom with everything that kings need.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: he was the most powerful of the people of the world in authority.

Al-Suddi said: he would be guarded every day by four thousand (men).

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: It has reached me that his guard every night was thirty-three thousand, whose turn did not come round to the same men until the following year.

Others said: forty thousand, equipped with weapons. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, through the narration of ʿIlba ibn Ahmar, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that two men from the Children of Israel brought a dispute to Dawud (peace be upon him), one accusing the other of seizing his cattle by force. The other denied it, and the accuser had no evidence. So (Dawud) postponed their case. When it was night, Dawud (peace be upon him) was commanded in a dream to kill the accuser. When it was day, he summoned them both and ordered the accuser to be killed. He said: "O Prophet of God, why do you kill me, when this man has seized my cattle by force?" He said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to kill you, so I will certainly kill you." He said: "By God, O Prophet of God, God has not commanded you to kill me because of this claim I have made against him. I am truthful in what I have claimed, but I had previously lured his father away and killed him, and no one noticed this." So Dawud (peace be upon him) [[Addition from S, T, A.]] ordered him, and he was killed.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: his awe grew among the Children of Israel, and this is what God, the Mighty and Majestic, means by: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾.

* *

God's saying: ﴿And We gave him wisdom﴾. Mujahid said: this means understanding, reason and perceptiveness. At another time he said: wisdom and justice. At another time he said: correctness.

Qatadah said: the Book of God and following what is in it.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿wisdom﴾ means prophethood.

* *

God's saying: ﴿and decisive speech﴾. Shurayh al-Qadi and al-Shaʿbi said: decisive speech means the witnesses and the oaths.

Qatadah said: two witnesses against the claimant, or the oath of the defendant, is the decisive speech by which the prophets and messengers made judgments, or he said: the believers and the righteous. It is the judgment of this community until the Day of Resurrection. Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami also said this.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: it is correctness in judgment and its understanding.

Mujahid also said: it is the decisiveness in speech and in ruling. [[In T: "in judgment and ruling".]]

This includes all of this, and it is what is meant; Ibn Jarir chose it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said [[In T: "and narrated it".]]: ʿUmar ibn Shabbah al-Numayri related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Abi Thabit related to me, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, from Bilal ibn Abi Burdah, from his father [[In T: "with its isnad".]], from Abu Musa (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The first to say 'Amma baʿd' was Dawud (peace be upon him), and it is the decisive speech."

Similarly al-Shaʿbi said: the decisive speech is "Amma baʿd."

* *

It is the judgment of this community until the Day of Resurrection. Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami also said this.

Mujahid also said: it is the decisiveness in speech and in ruling. [[In T: "in judgment and ruling".]]

Similarly al-Shaʿbi said: the decisive speech is "Amma baʿd."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 38, verses 17–20:

God mentions His servant and messenger Dawud (peace be upon him), that he was ﴿possessed of strength﴾. Al-ayd means strength in knowledge and in action.

[Ibn ʿAbbas] [[Addition from T, S.]] and Ibn Zayd and al-Suddi said: al-ayd means strength. Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿And the heaven We built with strength, and indeed We are expanding it﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47].

Mujahid said: al-ayd means strength in obedience.

Qatadah said: Dawud (peace be upon him) [[Addition from T, S, A.]] was given strength in worship and understanding of the religion. It has been related to us that he (peace be upon him) would stand in prayer for a third of the night and fast for half of the time.

This is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "The most beloved prayer to God is the prayer of Dawud, and the most beloved fasting to God is the fasting of Dawud. He would sleep half the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. He would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would not flee when he met (the enemy)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1131), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1159).]] And he was ʾawwab, meaning one who returns to God, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his affairs and matters.

* *

God's saying: ﴿Indeed We subjected the mountains to glorify (God) with him at evening and at sunrise﴾. That is, God subjected the mountains to glorify God along with him at sunrise and at the end of the day, as He said: ﴿O mountains, echo His praises along with him, and (you) birds﴾ [Saba': 10]. Likewise, the birds would glorify God in accordance with his glorification and echo his chanting. When a bird passed by him while it was gliding in the air and heard him chanting the recitation of the Zabur (Psalms), it could not go on; rather, it would stop in the air and glorify God along with him, and the lofty mountains would answer him, echoing with him and glorifying in accordance with him.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Misʿar, from ʿAbd al-Karim, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, [[In T: "with its isnad".]] from Ibn ʿAbbas [[In A: "Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both".]] that it reached him: that Umm Hani mentioned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest of Makkah prayed the forenoon prayer (duha) eight rakʿahs. [[In T: "Then he said".]] Ibn ʿAbbas said: "I had thought that this time has a prayer, and God, the Exalted, says: ﴿They glorify (Him) at evening and at sunrise﴾."

Then he related it from the hadith of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Safwan, from his client ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn [[In A: "from".]] Nawfal, that Ibn ʿAbbas used not to pray the forenoon prayer. He said: "I took him to Umm Hani and said: 'Tell him what you told me.'" Umm Hani said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon me in my house on the day of the conquest. He then ordered water to be poured into a bowl, then ordered a cloth, which he held between me and him, and he washed. Then he sprinkled a corner of the house and prayed eight rakʿahs. Their standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting were all equal, close to one another." So Ibn ʿAbbas went out saying: "I have read what is between the two covers (of the Qur'an), and I did not know the forenoon prayer until now: ﴿They glorify (Him) at evening and at sunrise﴾." And he used to say: "Where is the prayer of ishraq?" Afterwards he would say: "The prayer of ishraq." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/87).]]

Therefore He said: ﴿And the birds gathered﴾, that is, held back in the air, ﴿each one returning to Him﴾, that is, obedient, glorifying in accordance with him.

Said ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿each one returning to Him﴾ means obedient.

[And His saying] [[Addition from T, S, A.]] ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾, that is, We gave him a complete kingdom with everything that kings need.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: he was the most powerful of the people of the world in authority.

Al-Suddi said: he would be guarded every day by four thousand (men).

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: It has reached me that his guard every night was thirty-three thousand, whose turn did not come round to the same men until the following year.

Others said: forty thousand, equipped with weapons. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, through the narration of ʿIlba ibn Ahmar, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that two men from the Children of Israel brought a dispute to Dawud (peace be upon him), one accusing the other of seizing his cattle by force. The other denied it, and the accuser had no evidence. So (Dawud) postponed their case. When it was night, Dawud (peace be upon him) was commanded in a dream to kill the accuser. When it was day, he summoned them both and ordered the accuser to be killed. He said: "O Prophet of God, why do you kill me, when this man has seized my cattle by force?" He said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to kill you, so I will certainly kill you." He said: "By God, O Prophet of God, God has not commanded you to kill me because of this claim I have made against him. I am truthful in what I have claimed, but I had previously lured his father away and killed him, and no one noticed this." So Dawud (peace be upon him) [[Addition from S, T, A.]] ordered him, and he was killed.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: his awe grew among the Children of Israel, and this is what God, the Mighty and Majestic, means by: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾.

Similarly al-Shaʿbi said: the decisive speech is "Amma baʿd."

Tafsir of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 38, verses 21–25:

The commentators have mentioned here a story, most of which is taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources), and no hadith from the infallible one (the Prophet ﷺ) has been established regarding it that must be followed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a hadith whose isnad (chain of transmission) is not sound, because it comes through Yazid al-Raqqashi from Anas. Yazid, although he is among the righteous, is weak in hadith according to the imams. Therefore, it is preferable to confine oneself to merely reciting this story and to leave its knowledge to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the Qur'an is true, and whatever it contains is also true.

* *

And His saying: ﴿When they entered upon Dawud, and he was startled by them﴾. That was only because he was in his mihrab (private prayer chamber), which is the most noble place in his house, and he had commanded that no one should enter upon him that day. So he did not notice except two persons who had climbed over the mihrab wall upon him, meaning they surrounded him, asking him about their matter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and he overpowers me in speech﴾, meaning he overcame me. It is said: 'azza ya'izzu, when he subdues and overcomes.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And Dawud thought that We had tried him﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning, We tested him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and he fell down prostrating﴾, meaning he prostrated, ﴿and turned in repentance﴾. It is possible that he bowed first and then prostrated after that. It has been mentioned that he remained prostrating for forty mornings. ﴿So We forgave him that﴾, meaning what had come from him, concerning which it is said: "The good deeds of the righteous are sins for those brought near (to Allah)."

The imams, may Allah be pleased with them, differed concerning the prostration of Surah Sad: is it one of the obligatory prostrations (aza'im al-sujud)? There are two opinions. The new opinion (al-jadid) of the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, is that it is not one of the obligatory prostrations, but rather a prostration of gratitude (sajdat shukr). The evidence for this is what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said:

Ismail, who is Ibn 'Ulayyah, narrated to us from Ayyub, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning the prostration in Sad: "It is not one of the obligatory prostrations, but I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrate in it."

Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir also narrated it through Ayyub with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (sound and good)."

Al-Nasa'i also said at the commentary of this verse: Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan, who is al-Miqsami, informed us: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us from 'Amr ibn Dharr, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ prostrated in Sad and said: "Dawud, peace be upon him, prostrated it in repentance, and we prostrate it in gratitude."

Al-Nasa'i alone narrated it, and all the narrators in its isnad are trustworthy. Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, informed me by reading to him while I listened: Abu Ishaq al-Mudarraji informed us, Zahir ibn Abi Tahir al-Thaqafi informed us, Zahir ibn Tahir al-Shahhami informed us, Abu Sa'id al-Kanjarudhi informed us, al-Hakim Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us, Harun ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yazid Ibn KhunayS narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn Jurayj said to me: "O Hasan, your grandfather 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid narrated to me from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I saw in what the sleeper sees that I was praying behind a tree. I recited the prostration and prostrated, and the tree prostrated with my prostration. I heard it say while it was prostrating: O Allah, record for me with You a reward, make it for me with You a treasure, remove from me by it a burden, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dawud.'"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Then I saw the Prophet ﷺ stand and recite the prostration, then he prostrated, and I heard him say while prostrating what the man had related of the words of the tree."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Qutaybah, and Ibn Majah from Abu Bakr ibn Khallad, both from Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays (in a version: Yazid ibn Habish), similarly. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (singular); we do not know it except through this route."

Al-Bukhari also said at its commentary: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi narrated to us, from al-'Awwam, who said: "I asked Mujahid about the prostration of Sad, and he said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas: 'From where did you prostrate?' He said: 'Do you not recite: ﴿And of his descendants, Dawud and Sulayman﴾ [al-An'am: 84], ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90]. So Dawud, peace be upon him, was among those whom your Prophet ﷺ was commanded to follow. Dawud prostrated it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated it.'"

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zurayc narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, Bakr, who is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, narrated to us that he informed him that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri saw a dream that he was writing Sad, and when he reached the place where the prostration is, he saw the inkwell, the pen and everything in his presence turned over, prostrating. He said: So he related it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he continued prostrating in it afterward." Imam Ahmad alone narrated it.

Abu Dawud also said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from 'Ayyad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Sad while on the pulpit. When he reached the prostration, he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated with him. Then on another day he recited it, and when he reached the prostration, the people tensed up to prostrate. He said: 'It is only the repentance of a prophet, but I see that you have tensed up.' So he came down and prostrated, and they prostrated." Abu Dawud alone narrated it, and its isnad is according to the conditions of the sahih (authentic).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a nearness and a good place of return﴾, meaning: indeed, for him on the Day of Resurrection there is a nearness by which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will bring him near, and a good place of return, which is the lofty ranks in Paradise, because of his repentance and his perfect justice in his kingdom, as has come in the Sahih: "The just will be on pulpits of light at the right hand of the Merciful, and both of His hands are right, those who act justly concerning their families and what they are entrusted with." (Sahih Muslim, no. 1827, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the people most beloved to Allah on the Day of Resurrection and nearest to Him in position is a just leader, and indeed, the people most hated by Allah on the Day of Resurrection and most severe in punishment is an oppressive leader." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Fudayl, who is Ibn Marzuq al-Aghharr, from 'Atiyyah with this chain. He said: "We do not know it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet) except through this route."

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: I heard Malik ibn Dinar concerning His saying: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a nearness and a good place of return﴾, he said: "Dawud will be brought on the Day of Resurrection to the leg of the Throne, then He will say: 'O Dawud, glorify Me today with that beautiful, melodious voice with which you used to glorify Me in the world.' He will say: 'How, when it has been taken from me?' He will say: 'I will return it to you today.' He said: Then Dawud will raise his voice, with a sound that will exhaust the delights of the people of Paradise."

This is a command from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to those in authority to judge between people with the truth that He has sent down, and not to deviate from it, lest they stray from His path [in A: "the path of Allah"]. Allah, may He be exalted, has threatened those who stray from His path and forget the Day of Reckoning with a firm warning and a severe punishment.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father related to us, from Hisham ibn Khalid, from al-Walid, from Marwan ibn Janah, who said: Ibrahim Abu Zur'ah told me, and he had read the Book (the earlier scripture), that al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik said to him: "Shall the caliph be held to account, when you have read the earlier Book, and read the Qur'an, and gained understanding?" I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, may I speak?" He said: "Speak, under safe conduct." I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, are you more honoured by Allah, or was Dawud (David)? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gathered for him prophethood and the caliphate (khilafah), then He warned him in His Book, saying: ﴿O Dawud, We have made you a khalifah (vicegerent) on the earth, so judge between the people with truth, and do not follow desire, for it will lead you astray from the path of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the path of Allah...﴾ [the verse]."

Ikrimah said regarding ﴿For them is a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning﴾: This is of al-muqaddam wal-mu'akhkhar (inversion of word order, lit. "the preceded and the postponed"). The meaning is: For them is a severe punishment on the Day of Reckoning, because they forgot.

As-Suddi said: For them is a severe punishment because they neglected to act for the Day of Reckoning.

This view is more in keeping with the apparent meaning of the verse, and Allah knows best.

Allah, Exalted is He, informs that He did not create the creation in vain, but created them to worship Him and to affirm His oneness, then He will gather them for the Day of Gathering, so that He rewards the obedient and punishes the disbelievers. For this reason Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and that between them in vain. **Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 38, verses 30–33:**

He, the Exalted, says, informing that He bestowed Solomon upon David, meaning as a prophet, as He said: ﴿And Solomon inherited from David﴾, meaning in prophethood. Otherwise, he had other sons, for he had a hundred free wives.

* *

His saying: ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who often turned back (to Allah)﴾ is praise of Solomon, peace be upon him, for being abundant in obedience, worship, and turning to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Khalid narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, Makhul narrated to us, and he said: When Allah bestowed Solomon upon David, peace be upon them both, David said to him: "O my son, what is the best (thing)?" He said: "The tranquility of Allah and faith." He said: "What is the worst?" He said: "Disbelief after faith." He said: "What is the sweetest?" He said: "The mercy of Allah among His servants." He said: "What is the coolest?" He said: "Allah's pardon of people, and people's pardon of one another." David, peace be upon him, said: "You are a prophet."

* *

His saying: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, the poised, swift steeds﴾, meaning: when the poised horses were displayed before Solomon during his time of kingship and authority.

Mujahid said: They are the ones that stand on three legs with the tip of the hoof of the fourth; and al-Jiyad means the swift. Similarly said more than one of the early generations (salaf).

Ibn Jarir narrated: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Mu'ammal narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us from his father, Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, regarding His saying: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, the poised, swift steeds﴾, he said: "They were twenty horses having wings." Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Isra'il informed me, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, through his chain, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: "The horses that occupied Solomon, peace and blessings be upon him, were twenty thousand horses, so he slaughtered them." And this is more likely, and Allah knows best.

Abu Dawud narrated: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to him from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, through his chain, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived from the battle of Tabuk (or Khaybar), and in her alcove there was a curtain. The wind blew and uncovered a corner of the curtain, revealing Aishah's daughters' toys. He said: "What is this, O Aishah?" She said: "My daughters." He saw among them a horse that had two wings made of pieces (of cloth). He said: "What is this that I see in their midst?" She said: "A horse." He said: "And what is this that is on it?" She said: "Two wings." He said: "A horse with two wings?!" She said: "Have you not heard that Solomon had horses that had wings?" She said: "He laughed until I saw his molars, peace and blessings be upon him." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4932.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I preferred the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until (the sun) disappeared behind the veil."﴾ [In some copies: "said".] More than one of the early generations and the exegetes mentioned that he became occupied with reviewing them until the time of the afternoon prayer ('Asr) passed. What is certain is that he did not abandon it deliberately, but out of forgetfulness, just as the Prophet ﷺ was occupied on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) from the afternoon prayer until he prayed it after sunset. This is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) through more than one route. Among them, from Jabir, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came on the day of the Trench after the sun had set, and began to revile the disbelievers of Quraysh, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I almost did not pray the 'Asr until the sun was about to set." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, I have not prayed it." He said: "So we went to Buthan, and he performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it, and he prayed the 'Asr after the sun had set, and then prayed the Maghrib after it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4112, and Sahih Muslim, no. 631.]

It is possible that delaying the prayer for the excuse of a raid and fighting was permissible in their religion, since horses are intended for fighting. A group of scholars claimed that this was prescribed and then abrogated (naskh) by the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). Some of them held this view in a state of close combat and constraint, where neither prayer nor bowing nor prostration is possible, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did at the conquest of Tustar. This is reported from Makhul, al-Awza'i, and others. The first view is closer to correct, because He said after it: ﴿Bring them back to me," then he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: He said, "No, by Allah, I will not let them distract me from the worship of my Lord, the last of what (remains) with you." Then he ordered them, and they were slaughtered. Qatadah said likewise.

Al-Suddi said: He struck their necks and hamstrings with swords.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "He began to wipe the manes of the horses, and their 'araqib (hamstrings) are their ropes." Ibn Jarir chose this view and said: "Because he would not have punished an animal by hamstringing it and destroying some of his property without a cause, other than that he became preoccupied from his prayer by looking at them, and they bore no sin." What Ibn Jarir preferred in this is open to question, because it may have been permissible in their law to do such a thing, especially if it was out of zeal for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because he had become occupied with them until the prayer time passed. For this reason, when he gave them up for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, Allah compensated him with what is better than them, namely the wind that runs by His command gently, wherever he wished: its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course was a month's journey. This is swifter and better than horses. [This is the correct view; see al-Qurtubi's discussion in al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran (15/195, 196).]

Imam Ahmad narrated: Isma'il narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah and Abu al-Dahma' — and they used to travel often toward the House (the Ka'bah) — they both said: "We came upon a man from the desert dwellers," and the Bedouin said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand and began to teach me from what Allah had taught him, and he said: 'You do not leave anything out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah will give you something better than it.'" [Al-Musnad (5/78). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/296): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

He said: "What is the coolest?" He said: "Allah's pardon of people, and people's pardon of one another." David, peace be upon him, said: "You are a prophet."

* *

His saying: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, the poised, swift steeds﴾, meaning: when the poised horses were displayed before Solomon during his time of kingship and authority.

Mujahid said: They are the ones that stand on three legs with the tip of the hoof of the fourth; and al-Jiyad means the swift. Similarly said more than one of the early generations (salaf).

Ibn Jarir narrated: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Mu'ammal narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us from his father, Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, regarding His saying: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, the poised, swift steeds﴾, he said: "They were twenty horses having wings." Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, Isra'il informed me, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, through his chain, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: "The horses that occupied Solomon, peace and blessings be upon him, were twenty thousand horses, so he slaughtered them." And this is more likely, and Allah knows best.

Abu Dawud narrated: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah narrated to me, that Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to him from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, through his chain, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived from the battle of Tabuk (or Khaybar), and in her alcove there was a curtain. The wind blew and uncovered a corner of the curtain, revealing Aishah's daughters' toys. He said: "What is this, O Aishah?" She said: "My daughters." He saw among them a horse that had two wings made of pieces (of cloth). He said: "What is this that I see in their midst?" She said: "A horse." He said: "And what is this that is on it?" She said: "Two wings." He said: "A horse with two wings?!" She said: "Have you not heard that Solomon had horses that had wings?" She said: "He laughed until I saw his molars, peace and blessings be upon him." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4932.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I preferred the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until (the sun) disappeared behind the veil."﴾ [In some copies: "said".] More than one of the early generations and the exegetes mentioned that he became occupied with reviewing them until the time of the afternoon prayer ('Asr) passed. What is certain is that he did not abandon it deliberately, but out of forgetfulness, just as the Prophet ﷺ was occupied on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) from the afternoon prayer until he prayed it after sunset. This is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) through more than one route. Among them, from Jabir, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, came on the day of the Trench after the sun had set, and began to revile the disbelievers of Quraysh, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I almost did not pray the 'Asr until the sun was about to set." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, I have not prayed it." He said: "So we went to Buthan, and he performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it, and he prayed the 'Asr after the sun had set, and then prayed the Maghrib after it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4112, and Sahih Muslim, no. 631.]

It is possible that delaying the prayer for the excuse of a raid and fighting was permissible in their religion, since horses are intended for fighting. A group of scholars claimed that this was prescribed and then abrogated (naskh) by the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). Some of them held this view in a state of close combat and constraint, where neither prayer nor bowing nor prostration is possible, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did at the conquest of Tustar. This is reported from Makhul, al-Awza'i, and others. The first view is closer to correct, because He said after it: ﴿Bring them back to me," then he began to pass his hand over their legs and necks﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: He said, "No, by Allah, I will not let them distract me from the worship of my Lord, the last of what (remains) with you." Then he ordered them, and they were slaughtered. Qatadah said likewise.

Al-Suddi said: He struck their necks and hamstrings with swords.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "He began to wipe the manes of the horses, and their 'araqib (hamstrings) are their ropes." Ibn Jarir chose this view and said: "Because he would not have punished an animal by hamstringing it and destroying some of his property without a cause, other than that he became preoccupied from his prayer by looking at them, and they bore no sin." What Ibn Jarir preferred in this is open to question, because it may have been permissible in their law to do such a thing, especially if it was out of zeal for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because he had become occupied with them until the prayer time passed. For this reason, when he gave them up for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, Allah compensated him with what is better than them, namely the wind that runs by His command gently, wherever he wished: its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course was a month's journey. This is swifter and better than horses. [This is the correct view; see al-Qurtubi's discussion in al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran (15/195, 196).]

Imam Ahmad narrated: Isma'il narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah and Abu al-Dahma' — and they used to travel often toward the House (the Ka'bah) — they both said: "We came upon a man from the desert dwellers," and the Bedouin said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand and began to teach me from what Allah had taught him, and he said: 'You do not leave anything out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah will give you something better than it.'" [Al-Musnad (5/78). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/296): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim), surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 1 of 3):

He, exalted is He, says: "And We did test Solomon" (وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ), meaning: We tested him by depriving him of his kingship once. "And We placed upon his throne a body" (وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا). Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: it means a devil (shaytan). "Then he turned back in repentance" (ثُمَّ أَنَابَ), meaning he returned to his kingdom, his authority and his majesty.

Ibn Jarir said: The name of that devil was Sakhr. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah. It was also said: Asif, said by Mujahid. It was said: Asiru, also said by Mujahid. It was said: Haqiq (حبقيق), said by al-Suddi. They have related this story in both its extended and its abridged forms.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related from Qatadah, who said: Solomon, peace be upon him, ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis, and it was said to him: "Build it, and let no sound of iron be heard in it." He sought this but could not achieve it. It was said to him: "There is a devil in the sea called Sakhr, resembling a marid (rebellious jinn)." He sought him out. There was a spring in the sea that he would come to every seven days, so its water was drained and wine was put into it. When he came on the day of his visit and found the wine, he said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you corrupt the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he went away until he became very thirsty, and then he came to it and said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you corrupt the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance," and he drank it until it overcame his reason. He said: Then the ring was shown to him, or he was sealed with it between his shoulders, and he was humbled. He said: His kingdom was in his ring, and it was brought to Solomon, and he said: "We have been commanded to build this House, and we were told: let no sound of iron be heard in it." He said: Then the hoopoe's eggs were brought, and a glass was placed over them, and the hoopoe came and circled around it, seeing its eggs but unable to reach them. So it went away and brought a diamond, placed it upon the glass, and cut through it until it reached its eggs. Then they took the diamond and used it to cut stones.

Solomon, peace be upon him, whenever he wished to enter the privy (or the bathhouse), would not enter with his ring. One day he went to the bathhouse, and the devil Sakhr was with him, at a time when he had been intimate with some of his wives. He said: He entered the bathhouse and gave his ring to the devil, who threw it into the sea, and a fish swallowed it. Solomon's kingship was taken from him, and the likeness of Solomon was cast upon the devil. He said: So he came and sat upon Solomon's throne and his seat, and dominion over all of Solomon's kingdom was given to him, except his wives. He said: So he began judging among them, and they began to disapprove of many things from him, until they said: "The prophet of Allah has indeed been tested." There was among them a man who was compared to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab in strength, and he said: "By Allah, I will test him." He said: He said: "O Prophet of Allah" (and he did not see him as anything other than the Prophet of Allah), "one of us may be stricken with major impurity (janabah) on a cold night and deliberately leave off the ghusl until the sun rises. Do you think there is any blame on him?" He said: "No." He said: So while he remained like that for forty nights, the Prophet of Allah found his ring in the belly of a fish. He came forward, and no jinn, bird or other creature met him without prostrating to him, until he reached them. "And We placed upon his throne a body" (وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا). He said: It is the devil Sakhr.

Al-Suddi said: "And We did test Solomon" means: We afflicted Solomon. "And We placed upon his throne a body": He said: The devil sat upon his throne for forty days. He said: Solomon, peace be upon him, had one hundred wives, and one of them was called "Jaradah," who was the most favoured of his wives and the most trusted by him. Whenever he became impure or went to relieve himself, he would remove his ring, and he did not entrust it to anyone among the people except her. One day he gave her his ring and entered the privy, and the devil came out in his form and said: "Give me the ring." She gave it to him, and he came and sat on Solomon's seat. Solomon came out after that and asked her to give him his ring. She said: "Did you not take it before?" He said: "No." And he went out in his place, wandering. He said: The devil remained judging among the people for forty days. He said: The people disapproved of his judgments, so the reciters and scholars of the Children of Israel gathered and came to his wives and said: "We have disapproved of this. If this is Solomon, then his intellect has gone, and we disapprove of his judgments." He said: The women wept at that. He said: Then they came walking until they reached him, surrounded him, and then unfolded the Torah and read. He said: Then he flew from before them until he alighted on a balcony, with the ring with him. Then he flew until he went to the sea, and the ring fell from him into the sea, and a fish of the fish of the sea swallowed it. He said: Solomon came in his state, until he reached a fisherman among the fishermen of the sea, while he was hungry and his hunger had become severe. He asked them for food from their catch and said: "I am Solomon." One of them stood up, struck him with a staff, and wounded his head, and he began washing his blood while on the seashore. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him, saying: "What a wretched thing you have done by striking him." He said: "He claimed that he is Solomon." He said: They gave him two fish that had become foul among them. The pain of the blow did not distract him until he stood at the edge of the sea, split open their bellies, and began washing his blood, and he found his ring in the belly of one of them. He took it and put it on, and Allah restored to him his splendour and his kingship. The birds came and hovered over him, and the people recognised that he was Solomon, peace be upon him. The people stood apologising for what they had done to him. He said: "I do not praise you for your excuse, nor do I blame you for what has happened from you; this matter had to occur." He said: So he came and went to his kingdom, and he sent for the devil, who was brought to him. He commanded that he be placed in an iron chest, then sealed it, locked it with a lock, and stamped it with his ring, then commanded that it be cast into the sea, where it will remain until the Hour. His name was Haqiq. He said: And the wind was subjected to him, which had not been subjected to him before that, and this is His saying: "Grant me a kingdom such as shall not belong to anyone after me; indeed You are the Bestower" (وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنْبَغِي لأحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ).

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And We placed upon his throne a body" (وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا). He said: A devil called Asif. Solomon said to him: "How do you mislead people?" He said: "Show me your ring and I will tell you." When he gave it to him, Asif threw it into the sea, and Solomon wandered away, and his kingdom was lost. Asif sat on his throne, and Allah prevented him from approaching Solomon's wives, so he did not come near them, and they rejected him. He said: So Solomon would ask for food and say: "Do you recognise me? Feed me, I am Solomon," but they would deny him, until one day a woman gave him a fish, and he began cleaning its belly and found his ring in it. His kingdom returned to him, and Asif fled and entered the sea in flight.

All of these are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives from Israelite sources). Among the most objectionable of them is what Ibn Abi Hatim related:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Ali ibn Muhammad said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), regarding "And We placed upon his throne a body, then he turned back in repentance" (وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا ثُمَّ أَنَابَ). He said: Solomon wished to enter the privy, so he gave his ring to al-Jaradah, and al-Jaradah was his wife and the most beloved of his wives to him. The devil came in the form of Solomon and said to her: "Give me my ring." She gave it to him. When he put it on, the humans, jinn and devils submitted to him. When Solomon came out of the privy, he said to her: "Give me my ring." She said: "I have given it to Solomon." He said: "I am Solomon." She said: "You are lying, you are not Solomon." So he would not come to anyone and say, "I am Solomon," without being denied, until the children began throwing stones at him. When he saw that, he knew it was a matter from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: The devil then began judging among the people. When Allah wished to restore Solomon's authority, He cast into the hearts of the people the rejection of that devil. He said: They sent to Solomon's wives and said to them: "Do you disapprove of anything from Solomon?" They said: "Yes, he comes to us while we are menstruating, and he did not used to come to us before that." When the devil saw that he had been discovered, he thought his affair had come to an end, so they wrote books containing sorcery and disbelief, buried them beneath Solomon's throne, then dug them up and read them to the people, saying: "By this Solomon used to prevail over the people and overpower them." So the people declared Solomon, peace be upon him, a disbeliever, and they continued to denounce him. The devil sent the ring, and it was cast into the sea, and a fish swallowed it. Solomon used to carry loads on the seashore for wages. A man came and bought fish, among which was that fish with the ring in its belly. Solomon called out: "Will you carry this fish for me?" He said: "Yes." "For how much?" He said: "For one fish from this fish." He said: So Solomon, peace be upon him, carried the fish and set off with it to his home. When the man reached his door, he gave him that fish in whose belly was the ring. Solomon took it, split its belly, and the ring was inside it. He took it and put it on. He said: When he put it on, the jinn, humans and devils submitted to him, he returned to his former state, and the devil fled until he reached an island among the islands of the sea. Solomon sent for him, and he was a rebellious devil, so they began searching for him but could not find him, until one day they found him sleeping. They came and built over him a structure of lead. He awoke and leapt up, but wherever he leapt within the house, lead went with him. He said: They seized him, bound him, and brought him to Solomon. He commanded that a chest of marble be hollowed out for him, and he was placed inside it, then sealed with copper, then commanded to be cast into the sea. That is His saying: "And We did test Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body, then he turned back in repentance." He said: Meaning the devil who had been given power over him.

Its chain of transmission to Ibn 'Abbas is strong, but the apparent reality is that Ibn 'Abbas, if it is authentically transmitted from him, took it from the People of the Book, among whom there is a group that do not believe in the prophethood of Solomon, peace be upon him. It is therefore apparent that they fabricated lies about him. For this reason the narrative contains objectionable elements, the gravest of which is the mention of the women, for the well-known position is that the jinn was not given power over Solomon's wives; rather Allah protected them from him, as an honour and dignity for His Prophet (ﷺ). This story has been related at length from a group of the early scholars, such as Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Zayd ibn Aslam and others, and all of it is derived from the narratives of the People of the Book. And Allah knows best what is correct.

Ibn Abi Hatim said that Yahya ibn Abi 'Amr al-Saybani said: Sulayman found his ring in 'Asqalan, and then he walked in a rough woollen garment (in another manuscript: "in a garment of rags") to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), out of humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar a strange report describing the throne of Sulayman, upon him be peace. He said: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Misri informed me from Ka'b al-Ahbar that when he had finished speaking about "Iram of the pillars," Mu'awiyah said to him: "O Abu Ishaq, tell me about the throne of Sulayman ibn Dawud, what it was like, and what it was made of?" He said: The throne of Sulayman was made of ivory, inlaid with pearls, rubies, emeralds and jewels. A step of it was inlaid with pearls, rubies and emeralds. Then he commanded that the throne be surrounded on both sides by palm trees, palm trees of gold, whose fruit-clusters were of ruby, emerald and pearl. On the tops of the palm trees to the right of the throne were golden peacocks, and on the tops of the palm trees to the left of the throne were golden eagles facing the peacocks. On the right of the first step were two golden pine trees, and on its left were two golden lions, and on the heads of the two lions were two columns of emerald. On both sides of the throne were two golden vine trees that overshadowed the throne, and their clusters were pearls and red rubies. Above the steps of the throne were two great golden lions, hollow and filled with musk and ambergris. When Sulayman wished to ascend his throne, the two lions turned around for a while, then stopped and sprinkled what was in their hollows of musk and ambergris around the throne of Sulayman, upon him be peace. Then two golden pulpits were placed, one for his successor and the other for the chief rabbi of the Children of Israel in that time. Then seventy golden pulpits were placed in front of his throne, on which seventy judges from the Children of Israel, their scholars, and their distinguished and eminent men would sit. Behind all those pulpits were thirty-five golden pulpits on which no one sat. When he wished to ascend his throne, he placed his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne turned with what was on it and around it. The lion extended its right paw, and the eagle spread its left wing. Then Sulayman ascended to the second step, and the lion extended its left paw, and the eagle spread its right wing. When Sulayman had reached the third step and sat on the throne, one of those great eagles took the crown of Sulayman and placed it on his head. When it placed it on his head, the throne turned with what was on it, like a swiftly turning millstone. Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "And what turns it, O Abu Ishaq?" He said: "A golden dragon (tinnin) on the throne, and it is huge, made by Sakhr the jinn. When those eagles, lions and peacocks that are at the base of the throne sense its turning, they move up to the top. When it stops, they all stop, with their heads bowed over the head of Sulayman ibn Dawud, upon him be peace, while he is seated. Then they all sprinkle what is in their hollows of musk and ambergris over the head of Sulayman, upon him be peace. Then a golden dove standing on a column of jewel takes the Torah and places it in his hand, and Sulayman reads it to the people."

He mentioned the rest of the report, and it is very strange.

﴿He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me; indeed You are the Bestower.﴾ Some of them said: its meaning is that no one after me should be fit to take it from me, as happened in the matter of the body that was cast upon his throne, not that he was forbidding anyone after him among mankind. The correct view is that he asked Allah, Exalted, for a kingdom that would not be given to anyone after him among mankind like it. This is the apparent context of the verse, and the authentic hadiths have been related with this meaning through several chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Bukhari, in his commentary on this verse, said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Rawh and Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, an 'ifrit of the jinn escaped at me last night, or words similar to that, to cut off my prayer. But Allah enabled me to overcome him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that all of you could see him in the morning. But then I remembered the words of my brother Sulayman: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾." Rawh said: "So he sent him back in disgrace." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4808)

Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Shu'bah. (Sahih Muslim, no. 541; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11440)

Muslim said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, who narrated to me, Rabi'ah ibn Yazid, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to pray, and we heard him say: "I seek refuge in Allah from you," then he said: "I curse you with the curse of Allah," three times, and he stretched out his hand as if he were taking hold of something. When he finished the prayer, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we heard you say something in the prayer that we had never heard you say before, and we saw you stretch out your hand." He said: "Indeed, the enemy of Allah, Iblis, came with a flame of fire to put it on my face. So I said: 'I seek refuge in Allah from you,' three times. Then I said: 'I curse you with the perfect curse of Allah.' But he did not back off, three times. Then I wanted to seize him. By Allah, had it not been for the supplication of our brother Sulayman, he would have been bound, and the children of the people of Madinah would have played with him." (Sahih Muslim, no. 542)

Al-Imam Ahmad narrated: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Maysarah ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, Abu 'Ubayd, the chamberlain of Sulayman, narrated to us, who said: "I saw 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi standing and praying, so I went to pass in front of him, but he stopped me. Then he said: he narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to pray the Subh prayer, and he was behind him. He recited, and the recitation became confused for him. When he finished his prayer, he said: 'If you had seen me and Iblis, I swung my hand and kept choking him until I felt the coolness of his saliva between these two fingers of mine, the thumb and the one next to it. Had it not been for the supplication of my brother Sulayman, he would have been tied to one of the pillars of the mosque, with the children of Madinah playing with him. So whoever among you is able to prevent anyone from coming between him and the qiblah, let him do so.'"

Abu Dawud also narrated from it: "Whoever among you is able to prevent anyone from coming between him and the qiblah, let him do so," from Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, with it. (Al-Musnad 3/83; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 699)

Al-Imam Ahmad also narrated: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Rabi'ah ibn Yazid narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah al-Daylami, who said: I entered upon 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr while he was in an orchard of his at al-Ta'if called "al-WahT," and he was holding the hand of a young man of Quraysh who was accused of drinking wine. I said: "A hadith has reached me from you that: 'Whoever drinks a sip of wine, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept his repentance for forty mornings. Indeed the wretched one is the one who was made wretched in his mother's womb. And whoever comes to Bayt al-Maqdis, nothing brings him there except prayer in it, will come out of his sin like the day his mother bore him.'" When the young man heard the mention of wine, he pulled his hand from his hand and went away. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "I do not permit anyone to attribute to me what I did not say. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever drinks a sip of wine, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings; if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns again' (he said: I do not know whether it was the third or the fourth time), 'then it is a right upon Allah that He will give him to drink from the filth of the dead (radgh al-khabal) on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: "And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever is struck by His light on that day is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray. Therefore I say: the pen has dried up over the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'" And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Sulayman asked Allah, Exalted, for three things, and He gave him two, and we hope that the third will be ours. He asked for a judgment that would coincide with His judgment, and He gave it to him. He asked for a kingdom that would not be fit for anyone after him, and He gave it to him. And he asked that any man who leaves his house intending only to pray in this mosque would come out of his sin like the day his mother bore him. So we hope that Allah, Exalted, has given us that." (Al-Musnad 2/176)

This last part of this hadith was also narrated by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through chains from 'Abd Allah ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Sulayman, when he built Bayt al-Maqdis, asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for three qualities..." and he mentioned it. (Sunan al-Nasa'i 2/43; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1408)

It has also been narrated from the hadith of Rafi' ibn 'Umayr, may Allah be pleased with him, with a chain and wording that are strange. Al-Tabarani said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 3 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-Asqalani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla narrated to us, from Abu al-Zahiriyya [[In T: "And al-Tabarani narrated with his chain."]], from Rafi' ibn Umayr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Dawud (peace be upon him): Build Me a house on the earth. Dawud built a house for himself before the house he had been commanded to build. So Allah revealed to him: O Dawud, you have set up your house before My house? He said: O Lord, this is what You decreed [[In T, S, A: "Thus You said in what You decreed."]]: whoever becomes a king takes for himself first. Then he began building the Masjid, but when the walls were completed they collapsed, three times. He complained of this to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He said: O Dawud, you are not fit to build a house for Me. He said: And why, O Lord? He said: Because of the blood that was shed at your hands. He said: O Lord, was that not in Your pleasure and Your love? He said: Yes, but they are My servants and I am merciful to them. That grieved him, so Allah revealed to him: Do not grieve, for I will complete its building through your son Sulayman. When Dawud died, Sulayman began building it, and when it was completed he offered sacrifices, slaughtered animals, and gathered the Children of Israel. Then Allah revealed to him: I see your delight in the building of My house, so ask Me and I will give you. He said: I ask You for three things: judgment that agrees with Your judgment, a kingdom that should not be given to anyone after me, and whoever comes to this House intending nothing but prayer in it, let him leave his sins like the day his mother bore him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for two of them, he has been given them, and I hope that he has been given the third."
[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/24). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/8): "In it is Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Suwayd al-Ramli, who is accused of forging hadith."]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Umar ibn Rashid al-Yamami narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salama ibn al-Akwa' narrated to us, from his father, who said: I never heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) make a supplication except that he began it with "Subhan Allah, my Lord the Most High, the Exalted, the Giver" [[Al-Musnad (4/54). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/156): "In it is Umar ibn Rashid al-Yamami, whom more than one scholar declared trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

It has also been related by Abu 'Ubayd: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Salih ibn Misman, who said: When the Prophet of Allah Dawud died, Allah revealed to his son Sulayman (peace be upon them both): Ask Me for your need. He said: I ask You to make for me a heart that fears You as my father's heart did, and to make my heart love You as my father's heart did. Allah said: I sent to My servant and asked him what his need was, and his need was that I should make his heart fear Me and make his heart love Me. I will surely give him a kingdom that shall not be fitting for anyone after him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he willed﴾ and the verse after it. He said: So Allah gave him what He gave him, and in the Hereafter there is no reckoning for him.

This is how Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir cited it in the biography of Sulayman (peace be upon him) in his Tarikh [[Tarikh Dimashq (7/569), manuscript section.]].
