Ibn Abi Hatim said that Yahya ibn Abi 'Amr al-Saybani said: Sulayman found his ring in 'Asqalan, and then he walked in a rough woollen garment (in another manuscript: "in a garment of rags") to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), out of humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar a strange report describing the throne of Sulayman, upon him be peace. He said: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Misri informed me from Ka'b al-Ahbar that when he had finished speaking about "Iram of the pillars," Mu'awiyah said to him: "O Abu Ishaq, tell me about the throne of Sulayman ibn Dawud, what it was like, and what it was made of?" He said: The throne of Sulayman was made of ivory, inlaid with pearls, rubies, emeralds and jewels. A step of it was inlaid with pearls, rubies and emeralds. Then he commanded that the throne be surrounded on both sides by palm trees, palm trees of gold, whose fruit-clusters were of ruby, emerald and pearl. On the tops of the palm trees to the right of the throne were golden peacocks, and on the tops of the palm trees to the left of the throne were golden eagles facing the peacocks. On the right of the first step were two golden pine trees, and on its left were two golden lions, and on the heads of the two lions were two columns of emerald. On both sides of the throne were two golden vine trees that overshadowed the throne, and their clusters were pearls and red rubies. Above the steps of the throne were two great golden lions, hollow and filled with musk and ambergris. When Sulayman wished to ascend his throne, the two lions turned around for a while, then stopped and sprinkled what was in their hollows of musk and ambergris around the throne of Sulayman, upon him be peace. Then two golden pulpits were placed, one for his successor and the other for the chief rabbi of the Children of Israel in that time. Then seventy golden pulpits were placed in front of his throne, on which seventy judges from the Children of Israel, their scholars, and their distinguished and eminent men would sit. Behind all those pulpits were thirty-five golden pulpits on which no one sat. When he wished to ascend his throne, he placed his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne turned with what was on it and around it. The lion extended its right paw, and the eagle spread its left wing. Then Sulayman ascended to the second step, and the lion extended its left paw, and the eagle spread its right wing. When Sulayman had reached the third step and sat on the throne, one of those great eagles took the crown of Sulayman and placed it on his head. When it placed it on his head, the throne turned with what was on it, like a swiftly turning millstone. Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "And what turns it, O Abu Ishaq?" He said: "A golden dragon (tinnin) on the throne, and it is huge, made by Sakhr the jinn. When those eagles, lions and peacocks that are at the base of the throne sense its turning, they move up to the top. When it stops, they all stop, with their heads bowed over the head of Sulayman ibn Dawud, upon him be peace, while he is seated. Then they all sprinkle what is in their hollows of musk and ambergris over the head of Sulayman, upon him be peace. Then a golden dove standing on a column of jewel takes the Torah and places it in his hand, and Sulayman reads it to the people."

He mentioned the rest of the report, and it is very strange.

﴿He said: My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me; indeed You are the Bestower.﴾ Some of them said: its meaning is that no one after me should be fit to take it from me, as happened in the matter of the body that was cast upon his throne, not that he was forbidding anyone after him among mankind. The correct view is that he asked Allah, Exalted, for a kingdom that would not be given to anyone after him among mankind like it. This is the apparent context of the verse, and the authentic hadiths have been related with this meaning through several chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Bukhari, in his commentary on this verse, said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Rawh and Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, an 'ifrit of the jinn escaped at me last night, or words similar to that, to cut off my prayer. But Allah enabled me to overcome him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that all of you could see him in the morning. But then I remembered the words of my brother Sulayman: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾." Rawh said: "So he sent him back in disgrace." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4808)

Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Shu'bah. (Sahih Muslim, no. 541; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11440)

Muslim said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, who narrated to me, Rabi'ah ibn Yazid, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to pray, and we heard him say: "I seek refuge in Allah from you," then he said: "I curse you with the curse of Allah," three times, and he stretched out his hand as if he were taking hold of something. When he finished the prayer, we said: "O Messenger of Allah, we heard you say something in the prayer that we had never heard you say before, and we saw you stretch out your hand." He said: "Indeed, the enemy of Allah, Iblis, came with a flame of fire to put it on my face. So I said: 'I seek refuge in Allah from you,' three times. Then I said: 'I curse you with the perfect curse of Allah.' But he did not back off, three times. Then I wanted to seize him. By Allah, had it not been for the supplication of our brother Sulayman, he would have been bound, and the children of the people of Madinah would have played with him." (Sahih Muslim, no. 542)

Al-Imam Ahmad narrated: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Maysarah ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, Abu 'Ubayd, the chamberlain of Sulayman, narrated to us, who said: "I saw 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi standing and praying, so I went to pass in front of him, but he stopped me. Then he said: he narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to pray the Subh prayer, and he was behind him. He recited, and the recitation became confused for him. When he finished his prayer, he said: 'If you had seen me and Iblis, I swung my hand and kept choking him until I felt the coolness of his saliva between these two fingers of mine, the thumb and the one next to it. Had it not been for the supplication of my brother Sulayman, he would have been tied to one of the pillars of the mosque, with the children of Madinah playing with him. So whoever among you is able to prevent anyone from coming between him and the qiblah, let him do so.'"

Abu Dawud also narrated from it: "Whoever among you is able to prevent anyone from coming between him and the qiblah, let him do so," from Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, with it. (Al-Musnad 3/83; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 699)

Al-Imam Ahmad also narrated: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Rabi'ah ibn Yazid narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah al-Daylami, who said: I entered upon 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr while he was in an orchard of his at al-Ta'if called "al-WahT," and he was holding the hand of a young man of Quraysh who was accused of drinking wine. I said: "A hadith has reached me from you that: 'Whoever drinks a sip of wine, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not accept his repentance for forty mornings. Indeed the wretched one is the one who was made wretched in his mother's womb. And whoever comes to Bayt al-Maqdis, nothing brings him there except prayer in it, will come out of his sin like the day his mother bore him.'" When the young man heard the mention of wine, he pulled his hand from his hand and went away. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "I do not permit anyone to attribute to me what I did not say. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever drinks a sip of wine, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings; if he repents, Allah will accept his repentance. If he returns again' (he said: I do not know whether it was the third or the fourth time), 'then it is a right upon Allah that He will give him to drink from the filth of the dead (radgh al-khabal) on the Day of Resurrection.'" He said: "And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever is struck by His light on that day is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray. Therefore I say: the pen has dried up over the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'" And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Sulayman asked Allah, Exalted, for three things, and He gave him two, and we hope that the third will be ours. He asked for a judgment that would coincide with His judgment, and He gave it to him. He asked for a kingdom that would not be fit for anyone after him, and He gave it to him. And he asked that any man who leaves his house intending only to pray in this mosque would come out of his sin like the day his mother bore him. So we hope that Allah, Exalted, has given us that." (Al-Musnad 2/176)

This last part of this hadith was also narrated by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah through chains from 'Abd Allah ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Sulayman, when he built Bayt al-Maqdis, asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for three qualities..." and he mentioned it. (Sunan al-Nasa'i 2/43; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1408)

It has also been narrated from the hadith of Rafi' ibn 'Umayr, may Allah be pleased with him, with a chain and wording that are strange. Al-Tabarani said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 3 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Qutayba al-Asqalani narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla narrated to us, from Abu al-Zahiriyya [[In T: "And al-Tabarani narrated with his chain."]], from Rafi' ibn Umayr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Dawud (peace be upon him): Build Me a house on the earth. Dawud built a house for himself before the house he had been commanded to build. So Allah revealed to him: O Dawud, you have set up your house before My house? He said: O Lord, this is what You decreed [[In T, S, A: "Thus You said in what You decreed."]]: whoever becomes a king takes for himself first. Then he began building the Masjid, but when the walls were completed they collapsed, three times. He complained of this to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He said: O Dawud, you are not fit to build a house for Me. He said: And why, O Lord? He said: Because of the blood that was shed at your hands. He said: O Lord, was that not in Your pleasure and Your love? He said: Yes, but they are My servants and I am merciful to them. That grieved him, so Allah revealed to him: Do not grieve, for I will complete its building through your son Sulayman. When Dawud died, Sulayman began building it, and when it was completed he offered sacrifices, slaughtered animals, and gathered the Children of Israel. Then Allah revealed to him: I see your delight in the building of My house, so ask Me and I will give you. He said: I ask You for three things: judgment that agrees with Your judgment, a kingdom that should not be given to anyone after me, and whoever comes to this House intending nothing but prayer in it, let him leave his sins like the day his mother bore him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for two of them, he has been given them, and I hope that he has been given the third."
[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/24). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/8): "In it is Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Suwayd al-Ramli, who is accused of forging hadith."]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Umar ibn Rashid al-Yamami narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salama ibn al-Akwa' narrated to us, from his father, who said: I never heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) make a supplication except that he began it with "Subhan Allah, my Lord the Most High, the Exalted, the Giver" [[Al-Musnad (4/54). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/156): "In it is Umar ibn Rashid al-Yamami, whom more than one scholar declared trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

It has also been related by Abu 'Ubayd: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Salih ibn Misman, who said: When the Prophet of Allah Dawud died, Allah revealed to his son Sulayman (peace be upon them both): Ask Me for your need. He said: I ask You to make for me a heart that fears You as my father's heart did, and to make my heart love You as my father's heart did. Allah said: I sent to My servant and asked him what his need was, and his need was that I should make his heart fear Me and make his heart love Me. I will surely give him a kingdom that shall not be fitting for anyone after him. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he willed﴾ and the verse after it. He said: So Allah gave him what He gave him, and in the Hereafter there is no reckoning for him.

This is how Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir cited it in the biography of Sulayman (peace be upon him) in his Tarikh [[Tarikh Dimashq (7/569), manuscript section.]].

It has also been related from some of the early scholars that he said: It reached me that Dawud (peace be upon him) said: "My God, be for Sulayman as You have been for me." So Allah revealed to him: Tell Sulayman: It will be for me as You were for me, and I will be for him as I was for you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he willed﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: When Sulayman hamstrung the horses out of anger for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah compensated him with something better than them and swifter: the wind, whose morning journey was a month and whose evening journey was a month.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿wherever he willed﴾, it means: wherever he wished in the lands.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾, it means: among them were those employed in great constructions such as sanctuaries, statues, and basins like cisterns, and fixed cooking pots, and other arduous works that humans cannot perform. And there was a group who dove in the seas, extracting from them pearls, jewels, and precious things that are found nowhere else. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning those bound in fetters and chains from among those who had rebelled, disobeyed, refused to work, and turned away, or who had done wrong in their conduct and transgressed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account﴾, it means: this which We have given you of complete dominion and perfect authority, as you asked of Us. So give to whom you will and deny whom you will, and there is no reckoning against you. That is, whatever you do is permissible for you; judge as you will, and it is right. It is established in the two Sahihs [[The two Sahihs: the collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim.]] that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given the choice between being a servant-messenger, who does what he is commanded and is only a distributor who divides among the people what Allah has commanded him, and being a king-prophet who gives to whom he wills and withholds from whom he wills without reckoning or blame, he chose the first station after consulting Jibril, who told him: Be humble. So he chose the first station, because it is higher in rank with Allah and loftier in status in the Hereafter, although the second station, which is prophethood together with kingship, is also great in this world and the next. For this reason, when the Blessed and Exalted One mentioned what He gave Sulayman in this world, He also pointed out that he has a great share with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a nearness and a good final return﴾, meaning in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 38, verses 41–44:

Allah mentions His servant and messenger Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, and the harm with which Allah tested him in his body, his wealth and his children, until no part of his body remained healthy, not even the space of a needle's eye, except his heart. Nothing of the worldly means remained for him with which to seek help for his illness and his condition, except that his wife preserved her affection for him because of her faith in Allah and His Messenger. She would serve people for hire [[In manuscript A: "بالأجر" (bil-ajr).]] and feed him and attend to him for about eighteen years. Before that he had been in abundant wealth, children and vast worldly prosperity, but all of that was taken from him, until his condition reached the point that he was cast onto a garbage dump of the town, for this entire period, and both near and distant people abandoned him, except for his wife, may Allah be pleased with her. She would not leave him morning or evening except to serve people, and then she would return to him quickly. When the delay lengthened, the hardship intensified, the decreed destiny reached its end and the appointed term was completed, he humbly implored the Lord of the worlds and the God of the messengers, and said: ﴿Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 83]. In this noble verse he said: ﴿My Lord, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment﴾. It was said: "hardship" in his body and "torment" in his wealth and his children. At that point the Most Merciful of the merciful responded to him and commanded him to rise from his place and to strike the earth with his foot. He did so, and Allah caused a spring to gush forth, and commanded him to bathe in it, and it removed all the harm that was in his body. Then He commanded him, and he struck the earth in another place, and Allah caused another spring to gush forth, and He commanded him to drink from it, and it removed what was within his inner body of corruption, and his health was perfected, outwardly and inwardly. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink﴾.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab [[In manuscript T: "with their chain."]], from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the Prophet of Allah Ayyub, peace be upon him, remained with his affliction for eighteen years. Both near and distant people abandoned him, except two men who were among his closest brothers. They would come to him in the morning and the evening. One of them said to his companion: 'You know, by Allah, Ayyub has committed a sin that no one among the worlds has committed.' His companion said to him: 'And what is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah has not had mercy on him, so that He would remove what is upon him.' When they came to him, the man could not hold back until he mentioned that to him. Ayyub said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah knows that I used to pass by two men who were quarrelling and mentioning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so I would return to my house and make expiation for them, out of my dislike that they should mention Allah except in what is right.'" He said: "Ayyub used to go out for his need, and when he had finished it, his wife would hold his hand until he reached [home]. One day he was delayed, and Allah the Exalted revealed to Ayyub, peace be upon him: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink﴾. His wife grew impatient for him and went out looking for him, and he came toward her, Allah having removed from him the affliction, and he was in his best condition. When she saw him she said: 'May Allah bless you! Have you seen the Prophet of Allah, this afflicted one? By Allah, I have never seen a man more resembling him than you, when he was healthy.'" He said: "So I am he." He said: "He had two threshing floors, one for wheat and one for barley. Allah sent two clouds, and when one of them was over the wheat threshing floor it poured gold into it until it overflowed, and the other poured into the barley threshing floor until it overflowed." This is the wording of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him [[Tafsir al-Tabari (23/107). Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad (2357), Kashf al-Astar, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (3/374) through Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam from Nafi' ibn Yazid with it. Al-Bazzar said: "We do not know that anyone narrated it from al-Zuhri from Anas except 'Uqayl, and none narrated from him except Nafi', and more than one narrated it from Nafi'." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/208): "The narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the Sahih."]].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar related to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayra related to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'While Ayyub was bathing naked, golden locusts fell upon him, and Ayyub began gathering them into his garment. His Lord called to him: "O Ayyub, did I not make you independent of what you see?" He said: "Yes, my Lord, but there is no independence for me from Your blessing."'"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq with this chain [[Musnad Ahmad (2/314) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 278.]].

For this reason Allah said: ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding﴾. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Allah restored to him his family members themselves and added to them the like of them along with them.

* *

His saying: ﴿as a mercy from Us﴾ means: a mercy toward him for his patience, his steadfastness, his turning back to Allah, his humility and his submissiveness. ﴿And a reminder for those of understanding﴾ means: for people of intellect, so that they may know that the outcome of patience is relief, a way out and ease.

* *

His saying: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle and strike with it and do not break your oath﴾. This is because Ayyub, peace be upon him, had become angry with his wife and had resentment toward her over a matter she had done. It was said: she sold her braid for bread and fed him with it, so he blamed her for that and swore that if Allah cured him he would strike her a hundred lashes. It was also said that it was for other reasons. When Allah cured him and restored his health, it was not fitting that her reward, given her complete service, mercy, compassion and kindness, should be a beating. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave him a ruling that he should take a bundle, which is a cluster of stalks, containing a hundred stems, and strike her with it one blow, thereby fulfilling his oath, leaving his oath-breaking and keeping his vow. This is among the relief and the way out for whoever fears Allah and turns back to Him. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant, indeed he was ever turning back to Allah﴾. Allah the Exalted praised him and commended him, saying he was ﴿an excellent servant, indeed he was ever turning back to Allah﴾, meaning he was one who returns often and repents. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [At-Talaq: 2–3].

Many jurists have derived rulings on oaths and other matters from this noble verse and acted according to its implications. Another group of jurists refused this, and said: it is not established that expiation (kaffarah) was prescribed in the law of Ayyub, peace be upon him, so he was granted this concession; and Allah has made this Ummah independent of this through expiation.

Nothing of the worldly means remained for him with which to seek help for his illness and his condition, except that his wife preserved her affection for him because of her faith in Allah and His Messenger. She would serve people for hire [[In manuscript A: "بالأجر" (bil-ajr).]] and feed him and attend to him for about eighteen years. Before that he had been in abundant wealth, children and vast worldly prosperity, but all of that was taken from him, until his condition reached the point that he was cast onto a garbage dump of the town, for this entire period, and both near and distant people abandoned him, except for his wife, may Allah be pleased with her. She would not leave him morning or evening except to serve people, and then she would return to him quickly. When the delay lengthened, the hardship intensified, the decreed destiny reached its end and the appointed term was completed, he humbly implored the Lord of the worlds and the God of the messengers, and said: ﴿Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 83]. In this noble verse he said: ﴿My Lord, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment﴾. It was said: "hardship" in his body and "torment" in his wealth and his children. At that point the Most Merciful of the merciful responded to him and commanded him to rise from his place and to strike the earth with his foot. He did so, and Allah caused a spring to gush forth, and commanded him to bathe in it, and it removed all the harm that was in his body. Then He commanded him, and he struck the earth in another place, and Allah caused another spring to gush forth, and He commanded him to drink from it, and it removed what was within his inner body of corruption, and his health was perfected, outwardly and inwardly. Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about the virtues of His servants, the messengers and His worshipping prophets: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision﴾. By this is meant: righteous deeds, beneficial knowledge, strength in worship, and penetrating insight.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿possessors of strength﴾ means possessors of power, and ﴿and vision﴾ means understanding in the religion.

Mujāhid said: ﴿possessors of strength﴾ means strength in obedience to Allah, and ﴿and vision﴾ means sight of the truth.

Qatādah and al-Suddī said: they were given strength in worship and insight into the religion.

[And His saying] ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾. Mujāhid said: that is, We made them work for the Hereafter, having no concern other than it. Likewise al-Suddī said: their remembrance of the Hereafter and their work for it.

Mālik ibn Dīnār said: Allah removed from their hearts the love of this world and its mention, and purified them with the love of the Hereafter and its remembrance. Likewise ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: by "the Home" is meant Paradise; he means: We made it pure for them through their mention of it. In another narration he said: ﴿the remembrance of the Home﴾ means the final outcome of the Home.

Qatādah said: they used to remind people of the Home of the Hereafter and of working for it.

Ibn Zayd said: they were given, specifically, the best thing in the Home of the Hereafter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾ means: among those chosen and selected, the excellent. So they are excellent and chosen.

* *

His saying: ﴿And remember Ismāʿīl, al-Yasaʿ and Dhul-Kifl, and each is among the excellent﴾. The accounts of their stories and reports have already been discussed in full in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, in a way that makes repeating them here unnecessary.

The Most High informs of His believing, blessed servants that for them in the Final Abode is ﴿an excellent return﴾, which means the place of return and the final destination. He then explained it with His words: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning gardens of lasting residence, their doors opened for them.

The "al-" (definite article) here carries the sense of a possessive, as if he were saying: "their doors are opened for them." That is, when they come to them, their doors are opened for them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related: Muhammad ibn Thawwab al-Habbari narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Muslim, meaning Ibn Hurmuz, narrated to us, from Ibn Sabit, from Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn'. Around it are the battlements and the meadows. It has five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand houris. No one enters it, or, he said, dwells in it, except a prophet, a truthful one (siddiq), a martyr, or a just leader."

(Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. 1591, in Kashf al-Astar, through Muhammad ibn Thawwab with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/196): "In it is Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, and he is weak.")

Many hadiths have been transmitted about the eight doors of Paradise through numerous routes.

His words: ﴿reclining therein﴾. It was said: sitting cross-legged on couches beneath canopies, ﴿calling therein for abundant fruit﴾,

meaning whatever they request, they find and it is brought as they wish. ﴿And drink﴾, meaning of whatever kinds they desire, the attendants bring it to them ﴿with cups, pitchers, and a glass from a flowing spring﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 18].

﴿And with them are maidens restraining their gaze﴾, meaning they restrain their gaze from others than their husbands, so they do not look at anyone other than their spouses, ﴿of equal age﴾, meaning equal in youth and age. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, and al-Suddi.

﴿This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning﴾, meaning this is what we have mentioned of the description of Paradise, which He promised to His righteous servants, the Paradise to which they will go after their resurrection and rising from their graves, and their safety from the Fire.

The verses on this are very numerous.

﴿And with them are maidens restraining their gaze﴾, meaning they restrain their gaze from others than their husbands, so they do not look at anyone other than their spouses, ﴿of equal age﴾, meaning equal in youth and age. This is the meaning reported from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, and al-Suddi.

﴿This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning﴾, meaning this is what we have mentioned of the description of Paradise, which He promised to His righteous servants, the Paradise to which they will go after their resurrection and rising from their graves, and their safety from the Fire.

Then He informed about Paradise that it has no emptiness, no end, no cessation, and no termination, and so He said: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision; it has no depletion﴾, like His saying: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, but what is with Allah remains﴾ [an-Nahl: 96], and His saying: ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾ [Hud: 108], and His saying: ﴿for them is a reward never cut off﴾ [Fussilat: 8], meaning never cut off. And His saying: ﴿Its food is constant and its shade. That is the outcome for those who fear Allah, and the outcome for the disbelievers is the Fire﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 35]. The verses on this are very numerous.

The Most High informs of His believing, blessed servants that for them in the Final Abode is ﴿an excellent return﴾, which means the place of return and the final destination. He then explained it with His words: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning gardens of lasting residence, their doors opened for them.

The "al-" (definite article) here carries the sense of a possessive, as if he were saying: "their doors are opened for them." That is, when they come to them, their doors are opened for them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related: Muhammad ibn Thawwab al-Habbari narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Muslim, meaning Ibn Hurmuz, narrated to us, from Ibn Sabit, from Abdullah ibn Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn'. Around it are the battlements and the meadows. It has five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand houris. No one enters it, or, he said, dwells in it, except a prophet, a truthful one (siddiq), a martyr, or a just leader."

(Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. 1591, in Kashf al-Astar, through Muhammad ibn Thawwab with the same chain. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/196): "In it is Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, and he is weak.")

His words: ﴿This is a crowd rushing in with you. No welcome for them! They will indeed burn in the Fire﴾. This is a report of what the people of the Fire say to one another, as the Exalted said: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [al-A'rāf: 38]. That is, instead of greeting one another, they curse each other, accuse each other of lying, and disown one another. The group that enters first, when the group after it arrives with the guardians of Hell, the Zabāniyah (the angels of punishment), will say: ﴿This is a crowd rushing in with you﴾, meaning entering along with you. ﴿No welcome for them! They will indeed burn in the Fire﴾ [meaning: because they are among the people of Hell]. ﴿They will say: Rather it is you! No welcome for you!﴾ That is, the ones who entered will say to them: ﴿Rather it is you! No welcome for you! You brought it upon us﴾, meaning you called us to what led us to this destiny. ﴿Then how evil is the abode!﴾ meaning how evil is the dwelling, resting place and final destination.

﴿They will say: Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase his punishment double in the Fire﴾, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿The last of them will say to the first of them: Our Lord, these misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire. He will say: For each is double, but you do not know﴾ [al-A'rāf: 38]. That is, each of you has a punishment according to his state.

﴿And they will say: What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes turned away from them?﴾ This is a report about the disbelievers in the Fire, that they miss men whom they used to believe were misguided, meaning the believers in their assumption. They say: Why do we not see them with us in the Fire?

Mujāhid said: This is the saying of Abū Jahl. He says: What is wrong with me that I do not see Bilāl, 'Ammār, Ṣuhayb, so-and-so and so-and-so? This is an example given; in reality, all the disbelievers are in this state: they believe that the believers will enter the Fire. When the disbelievers enter the Fire, they miss them, do not find them, and say: ﴿What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes turned away from them?﴾, meaning in the world. ﴿Or have our eyes turned away from them?﴾ They console themselves with what is impossible, saying: Perhaps they are with us in Hell, but our sight has not fallen on them. At that point they will know that the believers are in the high ranks. This is His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? They will say: Yes. Then a caller will proclaim among them: The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾, up to His words: ﴿[And the companions of the heights will call to men they recognize by their marks, saying: Your gathering and your arrogance did not avail you. Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not bestow mercy upon them? Enter the Garden; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve]﴾ [al-A'rāf: 44–49]. [Added from T and S.]

All the angels complied with this, except Iblis. He was not one of them, but was of the jinn. His nature and disposition betrayed him at the very moment he most needed them. So he refused to prostrate to Adam, disputed with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about it, and claimed that he was better than Adam. He said that he was created from fire, while Adam was created from clay, and in his opinion fire is better than clay. He was wrong in this, opposed the command of Allah, and by this he disbelieved. So Allah removed him far away, humbled his nose in the dust, and expelled him from the gate of His mercy, the place of His intimacy, and the presence of His holiness. He named him "Iblis" to make known that he had despaired (ublisa) of mercy. He sent him down from the heaven, reproached and banished, to the earth. Then he asked Allah for respite until the Day of Resurrection, and the Forbearing One, who does not hasten against those who disobey Him, granted him respite. When he felt secure from destruction until the Day of Resurrection, he became defiant and transgressed, and said: ﴿Surely I will mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ As he said elsewhere: ﴿Have You considered this one whom You have honoured above me? These are the ones excepted in another verse, which is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them, and sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [Al-Isra: 65]

These are the ones excepted in another verse, which is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them, and sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [Al-Isra: 65]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said, "Then the truth, and the truth I say: I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together."﴾ Some reciters, including Mujahid, read "al-haqqu" (the truth) in the first place with a nominative ending (raf'). Mujahid interpreted it as meaning: "I am the truth, and I say the truth." In another report from him: "The truth is from Me, and I say the truth."

Others read both words with the accusative ending (nasb).

Al-Suddi said: "It is an oath which Allah swore by."

I say: This noble verse is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But the word from Me will be fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together.﴾ [As-Sajdah: 13], and like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense."﴾ [Al-Isra: 63]

Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: "I do not ask you for any wage for this message and this advice, which you would give me from the goods of this worldly life." ﴿And I am not of those who affect what is not theirs.﴾ That is: I do not add to what Allah sent me with, nor do I seek any addition to it. Rather, I convey what I was commanded, neither adding to it nor subtracting from it, and I seek by it only the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Last Abode.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-A'mash and Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: We came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "O people, whoever knows something, let him say it; and whoever does not know, let him say: 'Allah knows best' (Allahu a'lam), for it is part of knowledge that a man says of what he does not know: 'Allah knows best.' Indeed Allah said to your Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, and I am not of those who affect what is not theirs.﴾" It was related by al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of al-A'mash with this chain. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4809; Sahih Muslim, no. 2798.)

As for His saying: ﴿It is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ That is: the Qur'an is a reminder to all the accountable beings of mankind and the jinn. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il: Qays narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿to the worlds﴾, he said: "The jinn and the mankind."

This verse is like His saying: ﴿that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], and like His saying: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you will surely know its news﴾, that is: its report and its truth, ﴿after a time﴾, that is: soon. Qatadah said: "After death." And ʿIkrimah said: "That is, on the Day of Resurrection." There is no contradiction between the two statements, for whoever dies has already entered into the rule of the Resurrection.

Qatadah also said regarding His saying: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾: al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, at death the certain report will come to you."

End of the commentary on Surah Sad, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
